svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.27.10.2 Thickness
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.27 CLADDING
Thickness

g.text: Minimum thickness of OSB and waferboard cladding
Directly to framing or over furring strips
OSB, O-1 grade, and waferboard, R-1
OSB, O-1 grade, and waferboard, R-1
Directly to framing or over furring strips,
supports spaced not more than 400 mm (15¾″)
OSB, O-1 grade, and waferboard, R-1
Directly to framing or over furring strips,
supports spaced not more than 600 mm (23⅝″)
As printed, the two thickness columns sit under one heading, "Minimum
Thickness, mm". Forming Part of Sentences 9.27.8.2.(2) and 9.27.10.2.(2).
Note A-9.27.10.2.(2): In using Table 9.27.8.2. to determine the thickness
of Grade O-2 OSB cladding, substitute "face orientation" for "face grain"
Supports shown dashed behind the panel

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
OSB conforming to O-2 grade is not less than
6.0 mm (¼″) thick where applied directly to
sheathing.
OSB conforming to O-2 grade applied directly
to framing or over furring strips conforms to
the thickness shown for plywood in Table
OSB conforming to O-1 grade and waferboard
conforming to R-1 grade are not less than 7.9
mm (5/16″) thick where applied directly to
sheathing.
Where applied directly to framing or over
furring strips, OSB conforming to O-1 grade
and waferboard conforming to R-1 grade are not
less than
(a) 9.5 mm (⅜″) thick on supports spaced not more
than 400 mm (15¾″) o.c., and (b) 12.7 mm (½″)
thick on supports spaced not more than 600 mm
Table 9.27.8.2. as printed, metric only. Table A restates the Sentences of this Article. Strand pictograms in C are schematic.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.27.10.2. (page 9-266)
